title: Interception of registration data in transit identifies the parent
description: The flow carries directly identifying and highly sensitive attributes (email, full name, government ID) plus authentication secrets. If the transmission is not strongly protected, an eavesdropper on the network could identify the parent from the data in transit.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection is absent, weak, misconfigured, or terminated in an untrusted intermediary.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for identification via disclosure/interception in transit.

title: Network metadata can link the parent's registration attempt to the authentication service
description: Even if payload protection is used, flow metadata such as source IP address, timing, endpoint, and repeated retries can allow observers to link the parent user to this specific registration event and potentially correlate it with other activity.
assumptions: Assumes an observer can access communication metadata at the network, ISP, reverse proxy, or CDN level.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for linkability from communication metadata on a data flow.

title: Authentication service may collect more personal data than necessary for registration
description: The destination receives email, password, name, government ID, and a six-digit code in one registration flow. Collecting government ID at account creation may exceed what is necessary for authentication, creating a detectability/disclosure risk through unnecessary processing of sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Assumes government ID is not strictly required at this stage for the stated purpose of authentication/registration.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is framed as disclosure due to unnecessary collection/processing at the destination.

title: Sensitive registration data may be disclosed by storage or logging at the authentication service
description: On receipt, the authentication service may store or log email, name, government ID, six-digit code, and potentially mishandle the password. Application logs, debug traces, analytics events, or backups could expose these values to unauthorized parties or internal staff.
assumptions: Assumes logging, monitoring, backups, or database storage include raw request fields or insufficiently protected records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for data disclosure at the destination through storage/logging.

title: Parent may be unaware of how government ID and registration attributes will be used
description: The destination may process the submitted government ID, name, email, and code for purposes beyond immediate account creation, such as identity verification, fraud detection, analytics, or retention for compliance, without the parent fully understanding those uses.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices, just-in-time explanations, or consent/choice mechanisms are absent, unclear, or bundled.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of awareness/unawareness at the destination.

title: Registration may proceed without meaningful, specific consent for sensitive data processing
description: If the authentication service requests government ID and other personal data during registration without obtaining valid, specific consent or another clear lawful basis, the processing may be non-compliant. This is especially relevant for sensitive identifiers and any secondary uses.
assumptions: Assumes consent is the intended legal basis or that another lawful basis is not clearly established and communicated.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because compliance depends on jurisdiction and lawful basis.

title: Parent can later deny having submitted the registration data
description: If the system lacks adequate evidence of submission, the parent user may plausibly deny having sent the registration request or specific fields. This can create disputes around account creation, identity verification, or acceptance of terms tied to registration.
assumptions: Assumes the system does not maintain appropriate submission records, timestamps, or verification steps.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation issues caused by the act of sharing at the source.

title: Stored parent account records can be linked across contexts
description: When the users collection stores a parent account, persistent identifiers and stable attributes in the record can enable linking of the same parent across sessions, devices, child profiles, or other services if reused or correlated later.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account record contains stable identifiers such as email address, phone number, account id, device-related identifiers, or references to related profiles.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Parent account data in the users collection may identify the individual
description: The stored parent account is likely to contain directly identifying or quasi-identifying attributes, allowing the parent to be identified from the database contents.
assumptions: Assumes the account includes identifiers such as name, email, phone number, postal information, payment-related references, or unique usernames.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort estimate; exact LINDDUN Pro node may be more specific.

title: Stored account record may disclose sensitive parent information
description: Persisting the parent account in MongoDB can disclose personal data to unauthorized internal users, compromised components, or attackers if access controls, encryption, or segregation are insufficient.
assumptions: Assumes the record contains personal data beyond a bare opaque identifier, and that disclosure risk is in scope for storage and subsequent access.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree may differ depending on whether the taxonomy distinguishes storage disclosure from transfer disclosure.

title: Database contents may allow deduction of family relationships or account status
description: Even if some fields are not directly exposed, the structure and contents of the stored parent account can allow deduction of private facts such as the existence of children, household relationships, parental status, subscription status, or behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the parent account record includes links to child accounts, roles, timestamps, preferences, or service-usage metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro deduction subtree may be more specific.

title: Parent account data may be stored without sufficient user awareness or control
description: If the system stores the parent account without clear notice, understandable privacy information, or manageable settings, the parent may be unaware of what data is retained and for what purposes.
assumptions: Assumes transparency and user-control measures are incomplete or not effectively presented at account creation/authentication time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may distinguish lack of awareness from lack of intervention options.

title: Storage of parent account may exceed consented or expected purpose
description: The users collection may retain or reuse parent account data for purposes beyond those consented to or reasonably expected, such as analytics, profiling, cross-service reuse, or indefinite retention.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation, consent capture, or retention governance may be insufficiently enforced at the datastore.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact non-compliance subtree may vary by whether the issue is consent, purpose limitation, minimization, or retention.

title: Data flow metadata can link authentication events to a specific parent account
description: Even aside from payload contents, the act of sending a store-parent-account write to the users collection can create metadata such as timing, source process, destination collection, and operation patterns that link authentication events to a particular account lifecycle.
assumptions: Assumes logs, traces, network metadata, or database operation telemetry are available to observers or operators.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact flow-level linking node may differ.

title: Parent account data may be disclosed in transit to the datastore
description: If the flow between the Authentication Service and MongoDB is insufficiently protected, the parent account payload or associated metadata could be exposed during transmission through interception, logging, or misconfigured middleware.
assumptions: Assumes transport encryption, mutual authentication, and sensitive-data-safe logging may be absent or imperfect.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact disclosure-in-transit node id may differ.

title: JWT and returned user data can identify the parent user in transit
description: The flow carries a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If intercepted, observed in logs, browser history, referrer leakage, or other transit-adjacent channels, these values may directly identify the parent or make them identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT or accompanying user data contains direct identifiers, stable pseudonyms, or claims that can be tied to the parent user.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree numbering may differ.

title: JWT acts as a stable correlator enabling linkage across sessions or services
description: A JWT often contains a stable subject identifier, audience, issuer, or other claims. If reused or observable across contexts, it can allow linking multiple interactions of the same parent user across sessions, endpoints, or relying parties.
assumptions: Assumes the token is not strictly one-time, short-lived, and context-bound, and that claims or token values are observable beyond the intended recipient.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate; linkage clearly applies, but exact tree numbering may vary.

title: Parent user can learn more user data than necessary from the authentication response
description: The destination receives not only the JWT but also user data. If the response includes excessive profile attributes, account metadata, or claims not needed for the immediate purpose, the parent user gains unnecessary knowledge about the data subject.
assumptions: Assumes 'user data' may include attributes beyond what is strictly needed to complete authentication or session establishment.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability depends on what 'user data' contains; exact node id may differ.

title: Authentication response may be stored or reused by the parent user beyond the original purpose
description: Once the JWT and user data reach the parent user, they may be retained, copied, or reused for secondary purposes, creating a risk of disclosure dissemination beyond the original authentication transaction.
assumptions: Assumes the external entity can store, forward, screenshot, or otherwise redistribute the received token or user data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; dissemination at the recipient is the main concern.

title: Authentication service may share JWT claims and user data without sufficient transparency or valid consent basis
description: By sending a JWT plus user data to the parent user, the authentication service may disclose personal data in a way the data subject did not expect, was not informed about, or did not validly consent to, depending on the system's legal basis and notices.
assumptions: Assumes the returned user data relates to a data subject whose expectations, notice, or consent may not fully cover this disclosure to the parent user.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends heavily on context and governance; node id is approximate.

title: Parent email directly identifies the child account context
description: The child user submits a parent email address as part of login. This attribute can directly identify a household or parent-linked account, revealing identity information at the moment of disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the parent email is a real-world email address tied to a specific parent or household and is not a pseudonymous identifier.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for direct identification via explicit identifier disclosure.

title: Login transmissions can link repeated sessions to the same child or household
description: Repeated transmission of the same parent email and associated communication metadata over this login flow can allow an observer or intermediary with access to traffic metadata or contents to link multiple login attempts to the same child account or household.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker or internal observer can access network metadata, application logs, or repeated credential submissions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability across repeated observations of the same flow.

title: Login flow reveals use of the service by a child account
description: The existence, timing, and endpoints of the login transaction may disclose that a child user is interacting with the authentication service, even if credentials are protected, thereby revealing service usage.
assumptions: Assumes some party can observe traffic metadata such as source, destination, timing, or frequency.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability from communication metadata.

title: Authentication service can identify the child via received credentials
description: On receipt of parent email and password, the authentication service can resolve the login to a specific account and thereby identify the child user or household behind the session.
assumptions: Assumes the service maintains account records mapping parent email to a child account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identification performed by the recipient after account lookup.

title: Authentication service can link this login to prior and future activity
description: Because the same parent email/account credentials are reused, the authentication service can link this authentication event with previous and subsequent sessions, building a longitudinal picture of the child account's activity.
assumptions: Assumes account identifiers are stable over time and login events are logged or otherwise retained.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side linkability through stable account identifiers.

title: Authentication logs may create evidence the child cannot plausibly deny
description: If the authentication service logs successful or attempted logins together with timestamps and account identifiers, those records may later be used as evidence that the child or household performed a login, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes login attempts are logged and logs are retained with sufficient integrity to be relied upon.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for non-repudiation arising from audit logging.

title: Credential handling may enable unauthorized account access
description: If the authentication service inadequately protects the submitted parent email and password during processing or storage, unauthorized parties could gain access to the child account or associated parent account context.
assumptions: Assumes weak credential handling such as poor rate limiting, insecure storage, excessive logging, or improper access controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unauthorized use enabled by mishandling authentication credentials.

title: Collection of parent email for child login may exceed data minimization or child-privacy expectations
description: Using a parent's email address as the child's login identifier may process personal data about both child and parent in ways that could conflict with data minimization, purpose limitation, or child-specific privacy obligations if not strictly necessary and transparently justified.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy requirements impose heightened protections for children's data and require necessity and transparency for parental identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; non-compliance depends strongly on jurisdiction, age band, and service design.

title: Excessive disclosure of child profile data in authentication response
description: The authentication service returns not only a JWT but also child profiles. If more profile attributes are included than are necessary for immediate login completion, the source discloses personal data about a child beyond the minimum needed, increasing privacy exposure.
assumptions: Assumes the child profiles contain personal or account-related attributes not strictly required in the authentication response.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for over-disclosure/minimization failure at the source; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Identification of the child user from JWT claims or profile attributes in transit
description: The JWT and child profile data may contain direct or indirect identifiers such as account identifiers, usernames, profile names, avatars, or stable subject claims. If observed in transit, these can identify the child user.
assumptions: Assumes the token or profiles contain stable identifiers or identifying attributes and transport confidentiality could be weakened or metadata exposed.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id may differ depending on whether LINDDUN Pro separates direct vs indirect identification in transit.

title: Linkability via stable JWT subject or profile identifiers
description: A stable subject claim, account id, or profile identifier in the JWT or returned profiles can allow different sessions or observations of this flow to be linked to the same child over time.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are persistent across sessions or requests.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by persistent identifiers on the data flow.

title: Disclosure of sensitive role information that the user is a child
description: The flow explicitly conveys userType=child. Even if other identifiers are protected, revealing that the authenticated user is a child exposes sensitive categorical information that may warrant special protection.
assumptions: Assumes the role claim is visible in the token payload or otherwise inferable from the transmitted data.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is a disclosure threat focused on sensitive attribute exposure rather than generic over-sharing.

title: Insufficient transparency to the child about profile data returned after login
description: The child user may not understand that authentication returns both an access token and profile data, what fields are included, and how long they remain available on the device or client. This reduces user awareness and intervenability.
assumptions: Assumes the client UX does not clearly explain the returned data and its handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit usability/unawareness node; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Lack of clear necessity or valid basis for sending child profiles with authentication
description: Bundling child profiles with the authentication response may exceed what is necessary for login, creating a risk that the processing is not adequately justified, proportionate, or compliant with child-data protection expectations.
assumptions: Assumes some profile fields are not strictly necessary for authentication and no separate justification is established.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because compliance trees vary by legal-basis/necessity wording in different LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Parent discloses excessive child attributes during profile creation
description: The parent may provide more personal data than is strictly necessary to create a child profile, especially highly sensitive attributes such as government ID alongside name, date of birth, and gender. The act of sharing this full set creates a disclosure risk from the source side.
assumptions: Assumes not all listed attributes are strictly necessary for the initial child-profile creation use case.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for unnecessary/excessive disclosure at the source.

title: Child is identifiable from data in transit
description: The transmitted payload contains direct and strong identifiers or quasi-identifiers, including name, date of birth, gender, and government ID, which can identify the child if intercepted or observed in transit.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries these fields in readable form at some point in transit or in exposed metadata/logging.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for identifiability from data carried on the flow.

title: Parent-child records can be linked via the profile-creation flow
description: Because the parent is the sender and the payload concerns a child profile, the flow inherently creates an association between the parent account and the child identity. Observers of the flow or systems handling flow metadata may be able to link the child to the parent.
assumptions: Assumes sender identity, session metadata, or account context is available alongside the payload.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for linkability through communication metadata and contextual identifiers.

title: Sensitive child data may be exposed in transit or intermediary logs
description: Government ID and other child attributes may be disclosed not only to the intended recipient but also to intermediaries, monitoring systems, reverse proxies, or application/network logs if the flow is insufficiently protected or over-logged.
assumptions: Assumes possible exposure through transport, middleware, telemetry, or debugging/logging infrastructure.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate for disclosure during transfer or via transit-related artifacts.

title: Destination stores or processes more child data than necessary
description: Child Profile Management may retain or further process all submitted attributes, including government ID, even if some are unnecessary for profile creation, increasing confidentiality risk at the destination.
assumptions: Assumes P3 persists or reuses the submitted fields beyond the minimum needed for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for disclosure/exposure caused by destination-side storage or processing.

title: Secondary use of child identity data beyond profile creation
description: The receiving process may use the child's personal data for purposes beyond creating and managing the child profile, such as analytics, verification, personalization, or sharing with other internal services, without this being expected by the parent.
assumptions: Assumes purpose limitation is not strictly enforced at P3.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for destination-side use beyond the original purpose.

title: Insufficient transparency or consent for collecting sensitive child data
description: Collecting a child's government ID and other personal attributes may occur without sufficiently clear notice, granular consent, or age/guardian-specific transparency about why each field is needed and how it will be used.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or backend process may not provide adequate privacy notice or consent capture for each attribute.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; best-fit for non-compliance/consent-transparency issues at collection.

title: Parent may later be unable to prove or contest what child data was submitted
description: If the destination does not maintain appropriate evidence of what was entered, when, and under which parent account or consent context, the parent may be unable to repudiate or verify the submission, and disputes about the collected child data may be hard to resolve.
assumptions: Assumes auditability and receipt mechanisms are weak or absent.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation is less central for this flow; included as a plausible but lower-confidence threat with approximate node id.

title: Stored child profiles can be linked across contexts or over time
description: When the childprofiles collection stores persistent identifiers or stable attribute combinations, records about the same child can be linked across sessions, features, or datasets, enabling broader profiling than necessary.
assumptions: Assumes child profiles contain persistent identifiers or quasi-identifiers and may be queried together with other collections or historical records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Child profile attributes may directly identify a child
description: Storing profile data such as name, date of birth, photo, contact details, or unique account identifiers in the collection can make the child directly identifiable to parties with access to the datastore.
assumptions: Assumes the profile schema may include direct identifiers or uniquely identifying combinations of attributes.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate from memory.

title: Excessive profile storage enables disclosure of sensitive child information
description: The datastore may retain more profile fields than necessary, or retain prior versions on update, causing unnecessary disclosure risk if accessed, queried, exported, or breached.
assumptions: Assumes profile records may include sensitive or special-category data and that updates may leave historical copies, logs, or backups.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact subtree may vary.

title: Stored child profiles may be used for purposes beyond profile management
description: Once stored in the childprofiles collection, profile data may be reused for analytics, personalization, monitoring, or sharing with other components without being adequately limited to the original purpose of storing/updating the profile.
assumptions: Assumes secondary use controls and purpose limitation are incomplete or not enforced at the datastore/application level.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory.

title: Children or guardians may be unaware of what profile data is stored or updated
description: The act of storing/updating the child profile in the datastore may not be transparent to the data subject or guardian, leaving them unaware of the categories of data held, update behavior, retention, or downstream uses.
assumptions: Assumes limited notice, poor privacy UX, or lack of accessible explanations around profile persistence and updates.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate from memory.

title: Profile storage may occur without valid consent or other lawful basis
description: If child profile data is stored or updated without obtaining and recording appropriate parental consent, child assent where relevant, or another valid legal basis, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes the system relies on consent or another basis that must be demonstrable for child-profile processing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact node may differ.

title: Source process may send unnecessary profile fields to storage
description: The Child Profile Management process may write more attributes than are needed for profile management, increasing disclosure risk at rest and in subsequent use.
assumptions: Assumes P3 constructs write payloads and may include optional, derived, or legacy fields without minimization checks.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory.

title: Write-operation metadata can link profile activity to a specific child or account
description: Even if payload contents are protected, metadata on the store/update flow—such as record keys, timestamps, tenant/account identifiers, or operation patterns—can enable linking of repeated actions to the same child profile.
assumptions: Assumes flow metadata is observable in logs, traces, message envelopes, or database operation telemetry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory.

title: Repeated search/request/engagement data can link the child across sessions
description: The child user's searches, video requests, likes, and comments may contain persistent account identifiers or stable behavioral patterns that allow the same child to be linked across multiple sessions and interactions.
assumptions: Assumes the service can associate requests with an account, device, cookie, IP address, or stable interaction history.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability from repeated disclosures by the source.

title: Search queries, comments, or requests may identify the child directly or indirectly
description: Free-text searches, video requests, and especially comments may include the child's name, school, location, contact details, or other unique details that enable identification of the child.
assumptions: Assumes user-provided text fields are available and not fully constrained or sanitized before submission.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability through content disclosed by the source; exact node numbering may vary.

title: Communication metadata can link the child to specific viewing interests
description: Even if payload content is protected, metadata on the flow such as timing, frequency, endpoint, request size, and sequence of searches/likes/comments can be used to correlate the child with particular usage patterns or content categories.
assumptions: Assumes some observer or intermediary can access traffic metadata, or the service itself uses metadata for correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability via data-flow metadata; numbering is approximate.

title: Traffic metadata may reveal the child's identity or household context
description: Network-level metadata such as IP address, device identifiers, or routing information on the flow may identify the child or at least the household, enabling association of requests and engagement actions with a specific person or family.
assumptions: Assumes network or application metadata is visible to the recipient or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability arising from data in transit and metadata.

title: Searches, likes, comments, and requests disclose the child's interests and preferences
description: On receipt, the video management service can infer sensitive interests, habits, emotional state, developmental stage, or vulnerabilities from the child's search terms, requested videos, likes, and comments.
assumptions: Assumes the service stores or analyzes interaction history.

title: The service can link the child's actions into a detailed profile
description: The destination can combine searches, requests, likes, and comments over time to build a unified profile of the child, linking behavior across content categories, sessions, and possibly devices.
assumptions: Assumes the service maintains logs, account records, or device-level identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side linkability/profile construction; numbering is approximate.

title: The service may identify the child from account, device, or behavioral data
description: The video management service may identify or single out the child by combining submitted content with account details, device identifiers, IP history, or distinctive behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the service has access to account or telemetry data in addition to the flow contents.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for destination-side identifiability; numbering is approximate.

title: Collected interaction data may be used for secondary purposes beyond the child's expectations
description: The service may use search, request, like, and comment data for personalization, recommendation tuning, advertising, moderation training, analytics, or sharing with partners in ways the child does not expect or understand.
assumptions: Assumes purposes are broader than the immediate provision of search and video interaction functionality.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for unawareness due to opaque downstream use; exact numbering may differ.

title: Processing of a child's engagement data may not be transparent or validly consented
description: Because the data subject is a child, the service may lack age-appropriate notice, parental authorization where required, or another valid legal basis for collecting and processing searches, likes, comments, and requests.
assumptions: Assumes the system is subject to child-privacy obligations and that compliance controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance/legal-basis concerns; numbering is approximate.

title: The service may be unable to prove what the child actually submitted or whether actions were authorized
description: If likes, comments, or requests are logged without strong integrity, attribution, or parental authorization records, disputes may arise over whether the child actually performed the action or whether it was manipulated, undermining accountability for privacy-relevant processing.
assumptions: Assumes weak auditability or attribution controls for user actions.

uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; intended to capture detectability from record existence/metadata.

assumptions: Assumes notices/controls may not fully explain storage duration, downstream processing, or internal sharing.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

description: Persisting video files and metadata in the datastore without clear purpose limitation, minimization, retention limits, deletion support, or lawful basis can violate privacy obligations. Combining metadata and content may also exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Assumes potential gaps in retention/deletion controls, minimization, or purpose limitation for stored videos and metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; used as a general non-compliance category.

title: Detectability of transfers to the videos datastore
description: Traffic characteristics on the flow to MongoDB, such as timing, volume, frequency, or destination, may reveal when videos are uploaded, updated, or retrieved, allowing inference of user activity even if payloads are protected.
assumptions: Assumes an observer can monitor network or service-to-datastore interactions and infer events from metadata.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id for detectability via data-flow metadata.

title: Linkability via flow metadata between upload and retrieval events
description: Metadata on this flow, including repeated access patterns, record keys, object identifiers, or correlation IDs, may allow linking separate storage and retrieval events to the same user, video, session, or device.
assumptions: Assumes stable identifiers or observable patterns are present on the flow or in associated logs.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; intended to capture linkability from in-transit metadata.

title: Stored history can identify a child or household

title: Retention of detailed child history exceeds necessity
description: Storing full search and watch history in the childprofiles collection may collect or retain more personal data than is necessary for the stated purpose, especially if granular events, long retention periods, or broad reuse are involved.
assumptions: Assumes the system may retain raw history beyond what is strictly needed for immediate functionality.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for data minimization/retention concerns; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Secondary use of child history may be unclear or unexpected
description: Once stored in the childprofiles collection, search and watch history may be reused for analytics, recommendations, profiling, or other purposes not obvious to the child or guardian, reducing predictability and awareness of processing.
assumptions: Assumes purposes beyond immediate profile management are possible or not clearly communicated.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency about downstream use; exact node id may differ.

title: Storage of child behavioral history may be non-compliant with child-data obligations
description: Persisting children's search and watch history can conflict with privacy obligations such as purpose limitation, minimization, retention limits, heightened protections for children's data, or consent/parental authorization requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the service is subject to child-privacy or general data-protection requirements and stores behavior-level history.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and implemented controls; node id is a best-fit estimate.

title: Upload metadata can link parent activity across submissions
description: Even if video content is handled separately, metadata on the upload flow such as account identifier, device/network details, timestamps, and repeated submission patterns can allow linking multiple video uploads to the same parent user or household.
assumptions: The service can observe or retain transport/application metadata for uploads.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability via observable metadata on the data flow.

title: Video content or metadata may identify the parent or child in transit
description: The uploaded video and associated metadata may directly identify the parent user, child, home environment, school, location, or other unique attributes if intercepted or exposed while in transit.
assumptions: The flow carries raw video and/or descriptive metadata; transport protections may be absent, weak, or terminated in places that expose content.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability from data carried on the flow.

title: Video upload may reveal sensitive personal information beyond what is necessary
description: On receipt, the video management service may process or store highly sensitive content visible in the video, such as the child's face, voice, health indicators, religious cues, home interior, routines, or other special-category or intimate information not strictly necessary for approval/rejection.
assumptions: P2 stores or reviews the uploaded video for moderation/approval.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for disclosure of sensitive content at the destination.

title: Approval workflow may process excessive video data for the stated purpose
description: The destination may collect or retain full-resolution video, embedded metadata, thumbnails, and ancillary submission details when a smaller amount of data or shorter retention would suffice for approval/rejection, violating data minimization.
assumptions: P2 retains uploaded files and metadata beyond immediate decisioning needs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-minimizing collection/retention at the destination.

title: Parent may be unaware of moderation, retention, or secondary use of uploaded videos
description: If the service does not clearly explain how uploaded videos are reviewed, how long they are stored, whether rejected videos are retained, and whether content is reused for analytics or model training, the parent cannot remain adequately informed.
assumptions: Transparency notices may be incomplete or not presented at upload time.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient transparency/unawareness at the destination.

title: Parent may upload a child's video without valid or sufficiently informed consent/authorization
description: The act of sharing the video may occur without valid consent from all relevant parties, or without adequate parental understanding of the implications for the child's privacy, especially where the child is identifiable in the content.
assumptions: The uploaded video contains the child or other identifiable individuals and consent/authorization checks are limited.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for consent/non-compliance originating at the source; exact applicability depends on jurisdiction and system controls.

title: Service may be unable to prove what privacy notice or submission terms applied at upload
description: If the destination does not log the notice version, consent context, and approval/rejection actions tied to the upload, it may later be impossible to demonstrate what the parent was told or agreed to regarding processing of the video.
assumptions: P2 manages upload decisions but may not maintain auditable records of notice/consent context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation gaps around privacy-relevant submission events.

title: Child or household identifiable via stream metadata in transit
description: Even if the video content is approved, metadata on the stream in transit (such as device identifiers, account/session tokens, IP address, timing, or content-selection patterns) could identify the child user or their household.
assumptions: Assumes the streaming flow carries or is accompanied by network/session metadata observable by intermediaries or infrastructure components.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for identification via data/metadata in transit; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Viewing behavior linkable across sessions or services
description: Persistent identifiers or stable metadata in the video stream could allow different viewing sessions to be linked together, or linked with activity on other services, revealing a profile of the child user's interests and habits.
assumptions: Assumes reuse of persistent account IDs, device IDs, cookies/tokens, or stable network identifiers across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability caused by persistent identifiers in the flow; exact node id may differ in the official tree.

title: Disclosure of video content or metadata during transmission
description: If the stream or associated metadata is insufficiently protected in transit, unauthorized parties could observe the approved video being watched, the child's viewing choices, or related account/session information.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection may be absent, weak, misconfigured, or terminated at untrusted intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for interception/eavesdropping on a data flow; exact node id may vary.

title: Source discloses more child-related data than necessary in the stream
description: The Video Management Service may include unnecessary personal data alongside the approved video, such as precise account identifiers, recommendation context, internal classification labels, or tracking parameters, causing excessive disclosure to the child device/user environment.
assumptions: Assumes the service can embed or attach ancillary metadata beyond what is strictly needed to render the video.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit for over-disclosure/data minimization failure at the sender; exact official node may differ.

description: Once received, the stream may be exposed on the child user's device through local caching, screen visibility, notifications, or access by other apps/users on the device, disclosing what the child is watching.

title: Child may be unaware of tracking or personalization implied by streaming
